deviations: Access: web.archive.org was unreachable by curl (sandbox), by WebFetch (blocked) and by the browser pane (navigation denied); fs.knesset.gov.il redirects to a geo-block page; nevo.co.il (both the law_html pages and the Law_word gazette PDFs) now sits behind a one-time-code login; archive.ph, gov.il/apps/elections, hamichlol.org.il and albawaba.com returned blocks or 403. As a result none of the twelve gazette texts linked in the sheet could be opened; texts were taken instead from he.wikisource.org consolidated pages (read in full in the browser pane for the Knesset, Freedom of Occupation and Judiciary laws), from WIPO Lex consolidated texts with amendment notes (wipo.int/wipolex, texts 385541 and 385543; a mirror of the enactments' consolidated text, not on the permitted list by name), from search-result snippets of the indexed Knesset PDFs, and from Knesset committee protocols hosted by Open Knesset (production.oknesset.org), which are Knesset records.

Not found: the texts of seq 39 (Government, January 1996), seq 54 (Government Amendment No. 8, January 1999) and seq 61 (Government Amendment No. 10, December 2000) could not be read in any form; seq 61's content rests on dated press reports and Knesset committee records; seq 45's content rests on the Knesset Constitution Committee protocol of the day of passage. Those four cells are coded No because no closed-list fact was established, not because the texts were examined.

Working folder: WebFetch saved binary downloads (Word protocols, two PDFs) into the session's tool-results folder outside the fresh scratch subfolder; each was copied into the scratch subfolder circ-b2/dl for text conversion. No other folder was listed, opened or searched.

Secondary sources used only to look for leads, not as the basis of any code: the Hebrew Wikipedia article on the 1992 Basic Law: The Government (no 1996 amendment described); an IDI survey article on Basic Law amendments (no entries for these years); Jewish Virtual Library pages (Knesset highlights for the 13th and 14th Knessets, and a page reproducing a Jerusalem Post report of 19.12.2000, which is the press source cited for seq 61); an MFA election page surfaced only in a search summary. A Christian Science Monitor brief of 14.12.2000 and a Yated Ne'eman report of 20.12.2000 (press) were read for seq 61.

Page closed: a PDF fetched from idi.org.il under the title incapacitation-of-prime-minister-response-of-knesset turned out to be a 2023 High Court petition (HCJ 2412/23 and 2466/23 on Prime Minister incapacity, unrelated to any sampled enactment); I read only its first lines and three grep hits on ממלא מקום, then deleted it. A Word file fetched as a possible protocol on Amendment No. 6 was the 1991 Constitution Committee protocol on the original direct-election bill; another, on a bill numbered Amendment No. 8, was the 30.11.1994 Constitution Committee protocol on an amendment to the 1968 law. Both were set aside.

Court outcomes that reached me through search-result summaries or snippets without opening the page: (a) for seq 54, a Globes item summarized as a High Court ruling about the Central Elections Committee chair and the Knesset's term that attributes an interpretive difficulty to an omission in Amendment No. 8; not opened, not used; (b) for seq 48/51, a snippet describing the 22.10.1993 High Court ruling on meat-import licences under the 1992 Basic Law: Freedom of Occupation, and an IDI snippet about a 1997 ruling on investment-portfolio licensing; neither concerns a sampled enactment and neither was opened; (c) the he.wikisource.org Judiciary page itself carries a note that Amendment No. 3 (2023, section 15(d1)) was voided in HCJ 5658/23; not a sampled enactment, read only as part of the page text.

Numbering: WIPO Lex numbers the Knesset law at ס״ח 1565 עמ׳ 100 (seq 42) as Amendment No. 20 amending section 11, and the laws of 27.2.1996 (ס״ח 1566 עמ׳ 106) and 29.2.1996 (ס״ח 1568 עמ׳ 112) as Nos. 19 and 21 adding section 5A; the Wikisource markers do not state page assignments. WIPO Lex numbers the President law at ס״ח 1809 עמ׳ 2 (seq 67) as No. 5, recorded as originally numbered 6. For seq 45 the Constitution Committee's own numbering of the three Government amendment bills approved on 28.2.1996 (4, 5, 6) was stated to be provisional.

Budget: about 80 tool calls were used; no dedicated press search for a pending matter was run for seq 64 and seq 67, whose provisions are consequential drafting, nor beyond one search each for seq 58, 70 and 73.
